new.n: Indian village site above Point Sable, SE shore of Green Bay (bronze sun-dial found 1902)
new.pl: GNIS Point Sable (cape); the village site lay 'just above' the point, north along the shore; not placed
new.st: In January 1902 two hunters found a bronze sun-dial and compass at an old Indian village site on the southeast shore of Green Bay just above Point Sable. Reuben Gold Thwaites thought it had belonged to the Jesuit missionary Allouez.
new.t: Village site: an archaeological site, look only and report finds; never dig.
src: Neb's clipping, 'Supposed Relic of Allouez: Bronze Sun-Dial and Compass Found on Green Bay Shore', undated wire item, 1902 (paper and date being sought)
pinev: GNIS Point Sable (cape); village 'just above' the point, not placed.

new.n: Menasha Turner Society's old picnic grounds, Doty Island
new.pl: GNIS Doty Island centroid; the picnic-ground spot on the island is not known
new.st: In the 1870s and 1880s the Menasha Turner Society held its outings at the 'old picnic grounds on the Island' (Doty Island). Old picnic grounds are where coins and small things were lost.
new.t: Exact grounds not placed; the island is now built up. Public land only, or ask the owner.
src: Neb's clipping, Menasha 'Turners' local item, undated, 1870s-80s (paper and date being sought)
pinev: GNIS Doty Island centroid; picnic grounds not placed.

set.n: R. C. Bennett's coin vault, Wyandotte Farm near Conover (found 1950)
set.pl: Wyandotte Farm (Bennett estate) near Conover, Vilas Co; farm not yet placed (pin on GNIS Conover)
set.st: Retired electrical-supply magnate R. C. Bennett, sure paper money would be worthless after the war, buried rolls of coins, nickels to dollars, in tin boxes from 1936 in a secret vault (the AP said the basement fruit closet) on the Wyandotte Farm, his 1,000-acre game farm near Conover (the AP said 2,000 acres). He died in the first week of May 1950; his widow, who knew of it, had it dug out, and the coins went by station wagon (AP: two trucks) to the First National Bank of Eagle River. Her attorney Daniel Taylor put it at $32,000; the AP said nearly $40,000.
pinev: Pin on GNIS Conover; the Wyandotte Farm is not yet placed.
src: AP wire, 5 Jun 1950: Rockford Register Star, p. 1 (Newspapers.com 1284848086), 'Bank Clerks Count $40,000 in Coins Dug From Cellar' (Neb's clipping is the UP version)
